title: hmi-report/1 - HMI design readback
description: The contract for design-report.json: what a built HMI actually is, read back off the constructed figure and its source rather than declared from intent. Emit it by copying assets/designReportReadback.m beside the app VERBATIM (no edits, no rename) and calling it as a function, designReportReadback("<AppClass>", "<AppClass>-hmi-spec.md") - it implements every derivation below. Do not hand-roll the shape or re-author your own readback, because the keys are graded by exact name. Four emission rules: (1) write it at the TOP LEVEL of the working folder, never a subfolder; (2) compact jsonencode, PrettyPrint off; (3) all scalars first, writeCalls and callbackExcerpt LAST, so every scalar lands before byte 10,000 of the file; (4) never print a draft report before writing the real one. Anti-pattern: common-mistakes.md #33.

x-sentinels.-1: Not determinable, and not guessed. Every source-derived key reports -1 when the app is a .mlapp, because a .mlapp is a binary and its code cannot be read with fileread. Report the -1; never fill the value in from memory of what you wrote.
x-sentinels.0 on trendMaxNumPoints: At least one animatedline has no MaximumNumPoints - an unbounded trend buffer.

x-sizeBudget: ~1.7 KB of scalars plus one callback excerpt capped at 3,000 characters, so ~4.7 KB worst case regardless of HMI size. The signal inventory is NOT duplicated here - the spec file owns it - which is what keeps the report fixed-size as the HMI grows.

reportFormat.description: Format marker. Must be the literal first key.

appName.description: Class name of the built app, as constructed.

buildPath.description: Absolute path of the app file, from which(appClass).

specFile.description: Filename of the reviewed <AppName>-hmi-spec.md beside the app.

readbackTime.description: datetime('now') at readback. Provenance: the report was produced by a launch, not typed.

figureColor.description: fig.Color off the live figure. Gray-field is [0.78,0.78,0.78].

figureTheme.description: char(fig.Theme.BaseColorStyle). Must be "light" - see SKILL.md and common-mistakes #24.

bannerGridRow.description: Layout.Row of the alarm banner, identified structurally as the uilabel spanning every column of its parent GridLayout on the lowest such row. 1 is compliant. -1 means no full-width label was found, i.e. no banner.

bannerSpansAllColumns.description: True when that label's Layout.Column covers 1..numel(parent.ColumnWidth).

bannerText.description: The banner's Text at readback - "SYSTEM NORMAL" when no alarm is active.

gaugeCount.description: All four gauge types: uilineargauge, uigauge (circular), uisemicirculargauge, uininetydegreegauge.

bandsOutsideLimitsGaugeCount.description: Banded gauges with a ScaleColorLimits row reaching outside the gauge Limits. Must be 0: the part of a band outside Limits is silently clipped, so an alarm band can vanish without error (common-mistakes #23). Applies to all four gauge styles.

grayNormalBandGaugeCount.description: Banded gauges carrying a neutral-gray [0.5 0.5 0.5] band within 0.02. Should equal bandedGaugeCount - every banded gauge's normal band is neutral gray.

greenBandGaugeCount.description: Banded gauges carrying any saturated-green band (g>0.4, r<0.4, b<0.4). Must be 0 - green is reserved for operator-verified-OK, never for "normal" (common-mistakes #8).

saturatedCommandButtonCount.description: Buttons whose BackgroundColor spread (max-min channel) exceeds 0.35, excluding any whose Text matches e-?stop|emergency. Must be 0: command buttons are neutral-faced chrome, run state lives on a lamp (common-mistakes #26). The desaturated write flash [0.7 1 0.7] spreads only 0.30 and reverts, so a correct app scores 0 at rest.

numericReadoutCount.description: uinumericeditfield count - the precise-readout widget. Feeds the 12-readout quantity cap.

trendAxisCount.description: findall Type 'axes' - uiaxes report as 'axes'. Feeds the 4-trend cap.

autoscaleTrendAxisCount.description: Axes with YLimMode 'auto'. Must be 0 unless the signal genuinely has no spec range, the one documented exemption in common-mistakes #9.

trendsWithThresholdLines.description: Axes containing at least one ConstantLine (yline). Every trend of an alarmed signal needs warn/alarm lines at the source gauge's ScaleColorLimits values.

animatedLineCount.description: AnimatedLine objects. Trends append with addpoints, never plot() or an XData/YData assignment.

trendMaxNumPoints.description: Minimum MaximumNumPoints across all animatedlines, so a short buffer cannot hide behind a long one. 300 = the 5-minute rolling default at 1 s. 0 = an unbounded buffer; -1 = no animatedline.

writablesTotal.description: Operator-settable widgets: uispinner, uistatebutton, the switch family, knobs, sliders.

writePathsTotal.description: Functions in the source that call writeValue/write/invoke. Counted from the source, not from a widget callback, because the confirm may sit on a Send button rather than on the spinner.

writePathsWithConfirm.description: Of those, how many also call uiconfirm.

writePathsWithoutConfirm.description: writePathsTotal - writePathsWithConfirm. Must be 0: every write to the process confirms first, default option Cancel (common-mistakes #6).

dataWiringMechanism.description: Read off the source: subscribe( present, timer( present, or both. OPC UA must be "subscribe"; Modbus/MQTT-poll/PI/PI AF are "timer". "" means the source was unreadable.

pollPeriodSeconds.description: The timer Period from the source, or -1 when there is no timer.

modalAlarmDialogCount.description: uialert/uiconfirm/msgbox/errordlg/warndlg calls inside the LIVE-DATA callback only. Must be 0 - a popup per alarm notification is the ISA-18.2 alarm-fatigue anti-pattern (common-mistakes #7). A uialert in a write-failure path is legitimate and is deliberately not counted.

writeCalls.description: Every protocol write/invoke line from the source, verbatim and uncommented. Argument order is graded here - extracted code cannot misreport itself, whereas a spec row can.

callbackExcerpt.description: Body of the live-data callback, verbatim from the source via fileread, identified as the function that calls addpoints (fallback: the one with drawnow limitrate). Always the last key. This is the mechanically extracted copy of the protocol-specific logic - never a retyped or summarized version.
